Observational Astronomy.Optical and Near-Infrared Astronomy: Observations through visible and near-IR telescopes, imaging, photometry, spectral studies of stars, galaxies, transients; exoplanet detection (transits, direct imaging).
Observational Astronomy.Infrared and Mid-to-Far IR astronomy: Infrared telescopes and instruments (ground and space) examining dust, star-forming regions, galaxy evolution, protostellar disks, molecular clouds.
Observational Astronomy.Submillimeter and Millimeter Wavelength: Observations of cold gas, dust emission; studies of the interstellar medium, cosmic microwave background foregrounds; high-redshift galaxies via ALMA, etc.
Observational Astronomy.Radio Astronomy: Surveys of radio sources (galaxies, pulsars, AGN, HI mapping), fast radio bursts; radio interferometry; 21-cm cosmology; SKA pathfinder science.
Observational Astronomy.Ultraviolet Astronomy: Observations of hot stars, interstellar medium ionization states, galactic halos; space-based UV telescopes/instruments.
Observational Astronomy.X-ray Astronomy: High-energy processes: observations of black holes, neutron stars, supernova remnants, galaxy clusters; X-ray satellites, detectors characterization.
Observational Astronomy.Gamma-Ray Astronomy: Very high energy phenomena: gamma-ray bursts, active galactic nuclei jets, cosmic gamma background; ground arrays and space-based gamma satellites.
Observational Astronomy.Gravitational Wave Astronomy: Detection of gravitational waves from compact binary mergers, continuous sources; networks like LIGO, Virgo, KAGRA; instrumentation, data pipelines, and follow-ups.
Observational Astronomy.Neutrino Astronomy and Multimessenger As: Detection of astrophysical neutrinos; correlating neutrino signals with electromagnetic or gravitational wave signals; multimessenger campaigns.
Observational Astronomy.Time Domain and Transient Astronomy: Surveys and observations of variable and transient phenomena (supernovae, kilonovae, tidal disruption events, fast transients); real-time follow-up and multiwavelength coordination.

Planetary Science and Solar System Studi.Planetary Surface and Geology: Landed / orbiter imaging and spectroscopy of planetary surfaces; geology, tectonics, impact cratering; regolith studies.
Planetary Science and Solar System Studi.Atmospheres and Meteorology of Planets a: Remote and in situ measurements of atmospheric composition, dynamics, climate; cloud physics; aerosol/dust; meteorology on other worlds.
Planetary Science and Solar System Studi.Planetary Interiors and Magnetospheres: Gravity, magnetic field mapping; seismology (e.g. Mars, Moon); modeling and measurement of cores; studies of planetary dynamo effects; interaction with solar wind.
Planetary Science and Solar System Studi.Small Bodies and minor solar system obje: Asteroids, comets, Kuiper Belt / Centaur objects; sample return missions, telescopic observations of shape, composition, activity.
Planetary Science and Solar System Studi.Planetary Ring Systems and Satellites: Dynamics, composition, structure of rings; satellite geology, orbital interactions; tidal heating; sub-surface oceans in icy moons.
Planetary Science and Solar System Studi.Exoplanets and Planetary Formation: Transit and radial velocity measurements; direct imaging; atmospheric characterization; disk observations and theory; protoplanetary disks, planet formation processes.

Solar and Heliophysics.Solar Physics: Solar surface & atmosphere studies: sunspots, flares, coronal mass ejections; solar magnetic field measurements; helioseismology; energy transport in solar atmosphere.
Solar and Heliophysics.Solar Wind and Heliospheric Physics: In situ measurements of solar wind, particle acceleration, interplanetary space; heliospheric current sheet; interactions with planetary magnetospheres.
Solar and Heliophysics.Space Weather and Magnetospheric Science: Observations (satellites, ground) of how solar output affects Earth's magnetosphere; radiation belts; aurora; instrumentation to monitor space-environment effects.

Galactic and Extragalactic Astronomy.Stellar Astronomy and Star Formation: Observational programs of stellar populations; formation of stars; protostellar cores; stellar evolution stages; stellar multiplicity; cluster dynamics.
Galactic and Extragalactic Astronomy.Galactic Structure and Dynamics: Mapping our Galaxy's structure (disk, bulge, halo); kinematics and dynamics from surveys (Gaia etc.); interstellar medium structure; chemical abundances.
Galactic and Extragalactic Astronomy.Galaxy Formation and Evolution: Observations across cosmic time of galaxy morphology, star formation rates, mergers; surveys with large telescopes; environmental effects; quenching processes.
Galactic and Extragalactic Astronomy.Active Galactic Nuclei and Black Hole As: Observations of supermassive black holes; jets; accretion disks; feedback; AGN variability; reverberation mapping; high-energy emission.
Galactic and Extragalactic Astronomy.Galaxy Clusters and Large Scale Structur: Observations of clusters (mass, temperature, gas); weak and strong lensing; cosmic web mapping; cluster evolution; dark matter distributions.
Galactic and Extragalactic Astronomy.Interstellar and Intergalactic Medium (I: Studies of gas and dust between stars / galaxies; absorption / emission lines; cooling/heating, metal enrichment; Lyman-alpha forest; cosmic reionization.

Cosmology and CMB.Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) Observ: Measurement of CMB anisotropies, B-mode polarization, lensing; experiments like ground-, balloon-, and space-based CMB missions; foreground characterization.
Cosmology and CMB.Large Scale Structure Surveys: Galaxy redshift surveys, weak lensing surveys, clustering, baryon acoustic oscillations; mapping dark matter / dark energy effects over large volumes.
Cosmology and CMB.Dark Matter and Dark Energy experiments: Observational probes to constrain dark matter properties; gravitational lensing; supernova cosmology; large surveys; direct detection overlap (when astrophysical signals).
Cosmology and CMB.Cosmological Transient Events: Observations of rare, early-universe events—e.g. first stars, Population III; high redshift GRBs; reionization epoch; early galaxy formation.
Cosmology and CMB.21 cm Cosmology and High-Redshift Univer: Experiments observing 21 cm signals from neutral hydrogen; probing cosmic dawn / reionization; global signal and mapping with radio arrays.

Instrumentation and Laboratory Astrophys.Telescope and Detector Development: Design, calibration, and performance testing of imaging, spectroscopic, photometric, radio, IR, UV, X-, gamma-ray detectors; adaptive optics; large ground and space telescopes.
Instrumentation and Laboratory Astrophys.Laboratory Astrophysics: Measurements of atomic/molecular spectra, reaction cross-sections, dust grain properties under space-like conditions; opacity, equation of state; simulation of astrophysical environments in the lab. “Lab astro” to support interpretation of observations.
Instrumentation and Laboratory Astrophys.Flight Missions and Payload Experiments: Spacecraft / satellites / probes: mission design, in-situ sensors; remote sensing instruments; calibration; mission data acquisition and initial data processing.
Instrumentation and Laboratory Astrophys.Survey Instrumentation and Sky Surveys: Design and execution of large scale surveys (optical, radio, IR etc.); pipeline development; calibration; data systematics mitigation.
